Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the NovaGen Power Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaGen Power Corp.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Bradley, Chief Operating Officer; Karen Lee, Chief Strategy Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
1. Key achievements and challenges during the quarter.
2. Discussion of regulatory lag and mitigation strategies.
3. Grid modernization and smart grid initiatives.
4. Retirement of fossil fuel plants and replacement strategies.
5. Progress on our strategic initiatives and long-term goals.
6. Authorized vs. earned Return on Equity (ROE) analysis.

Let me provide some more detail on these six key aspects, starting with our progress on strategic initiatives and long-term goals. Good morning again, everyone. Before diving deeper into the numbers, I'd like to update you on our strategic initiatives, which continue to guide NovaGen Power Corp. toward sustainable growth and leadership in the evolving energy landscape. Our three-pillar strategy—Decarbonization and Clean Energy Transition, Grid Resilience and Modernization, and Demand Growth Capture—is set to deliver 8-10% annual EPS growth through 2030, while hitting our net-zero emissions target by 2045, ahead of peers like Duke Energy or Southern Company.

On Decarbonization and Clean Energy Transition, our top pillar, we've accelerated our renewables pipeline with tailwinds from the Inflation Reduction Act and growing corporate PPAs. In Q3, we reached commercial operation on 450 MW of utility-scale solar in ERCOT—our biggest single-quarter addition—pushing our total renewables portfolio to 12.5 GW, a 25% year-over-year jump. That includes the 250 MW Phase II expansion at Rattlesnake Solar in Texas, hitting a 32% capacity factor with First Solar bifacial panels and Nextracker single-axis trackers.

For wind, we're 85% done with the 300 MW offshore wind farm off Virginia in PJM, using Siemens Gamesa 14 MW turbines, positioning us for BOEM lease auctions with first power in H2 2025. Battery storage shines too: 400 MWh of long-duration units via Tesla Megapack 2XL at California sites, providing 4-hour dispatchable clean power to arbitrage CAISO's duck curve. Clean energy now makes up 48% of our mix—exceeding our 2030 target of 70% and matching NextEra levels. Emissions intensity fell 22% year-over-year to 350 grams CO2/kWh, on pace for 50% cut by 2030.

We deployed $1.8 billion in Q3 capex for renewables and storage, within a $7.2 billion annual plan, 60% IRA-tax credit eligible. ROIC tops 12%, supported by hedge collars at $45-55/MWh for 80% of new capacity.

Shifting to Grid Resilience and Modernization, reliability remains paramount amid extreme weather and cyber risks. We've finished 65% of our $1.2 billion Advanced Distribution Management System rollout with GE Vernova for DERMS integration, cutting SAIDI 18% in the Southeast, beating FERC standards. In Texas, post-Uri, we've added 200 MW dual-fuel H-class peakers from Mitsubishi Power for black-start.

Performance varies regionally but stays strong. ERCOT's data center load growth—up 15% YoY—has us landing 1.2 GW behind-the-meter deals with Google and Microsoft. PJM faces MOPR hurdles, but our 500 MW queue offers long visibility. In CAISO, 25% rooftop solar at peak is squeezing revenues, offset by 150 MW VPPs with OhmConnect yielding $50 million in ancillaries YTD.

Demand Growth Capture is thriving. EIA sees U.S. power demand at 4.5% CAGR through 2030 from EVs, reshoring, and AI data centers taking 8% of electricity. Our $500 million EV fund installed 5,000 Level 2 chargers in the Southeast at 65% utilization. Residential electrification enrolled 200,000 customers, lifting non-fuel revenues 12% YoY.

We're optimizing thermal assets: retiring 1.2 GW subcritical coal by 2026, converting 80% to natural gas with CCUS pilots via NET Power's Allam Cycle for 95% capture at $30/ton. M&A is opportunistic—we closed $400 million for 600 MW Midwest wind from Orsted in Q2, accretive at 9x EV/EBITDA.

Long-term, we target 25 GW clean capacity from today's 12.5 GW, $2.5 billion annual regulated ROE from grid spend, and 18% adjusted FFO-to-debt. Risks like HVDC delays or rate volatility are hedged with 70% fixed-rate debt at 4.2% and $3 billion liquidity. We're ahead, de-risked, ready to outperform as clean reliable power becomes key.

To cover the other aspects in more depth, particularly the financial and regulatory nuances, I'll turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez to discuss the financials.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. For Q3, we reported earnings per share of $0.92 and revenue of $2.45 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and disciplined capital allocation across our 25 GW fleet in PJM, MISO, and ERCOT.

I'll now dive into the key achievements and challenges that shaped our Q3 results at NovaGen Power Corp., operating this diversified fleet of thermal, nuclear, renewables, and storage assets. This quarter highlights our execution amid volatility from data center loads, Henry Hub gas at $3.25/MMBtu—up 15% quarter-over-quarter—and supply chain issues for transformers and solar modules.

Key achievements: Operationally, record adjusted generation of 18.2 million MWh, up 7.2% year-over-year and 4.1% above guidance, with 92.8% fleet availability—best Q3 in five years—thanks to maintenance on our 4.2 GW CCGT portfolio. Liberty Creek CCGT in PJM hit 95.4% capacity factor on $28/MWh spark spreads.

Renewables excelled: 3.8 GW wind/solar produced 2.9 million MWh, up 22% YoY, from Midwest wind adequacy and full ramp at 450 MW Desert Bloom solar-plus-storage in ERCOT. Capacity factors: 38% wind, 27% solar, aided by AI forecasting cutting imbalance penalties 18% or $4.2 million.

Strategically, closed $750 million Horizon Renewables 600 MW acquisition in MISO with Google/Meta PPAs at 4.8% IRR, 12-year terms, growing backlog to 5.2 GW. Pine Ridge 300 MW BESS hit ops early, 85% efficiency, $12 million ancillaries from ERCOT regulation—leading peers like NextEra in grid services.

Financially, adjusted EBITDA $425 million, up 11% YoY, beat consensus $15 million. O&M $112/kW-year, down 6% via Zero-Based Reliability digitizing 40% outages with GE Vernova Predix. Capex $320 million on nuclear uprates at 1.8 GW Seabrook, 15% steam generators done for 50 MW add by 2025.

ERCOT led with 14% hyperscaler growth, 25% more gas dispatch at 30% better margins than PJM. MISO coal-to-gas at Twin Oaks saved $18 million MATS, cut CO2 22%.

Challenges: Fuel to $1.42/MMBtu equivalent, up 12% QoQ, from 20% PRB coal spike impacting 2.1 GW coal at 10,200 Btu/kWh heat rates—80 bps margin hit, cushioned by 65% gas hedge at $2.85/MMBtu.

Regulatory: FERC delayed PJM 500 kV upgrade 90 days, shifting $150 million capex, risking $25 million wheeling. ERCOT ORDC at $45/MW-month below $55 breakeven, idled 200 MW peakers.

Weather: Midwest drought cut hydro 15% or 120 GWh; Texas hurricane outage 48 hours at Gulf CTs hiked lambda 8%. Supply chain: Siemens turbines to 28 months, delaying 1 GW CCGT six months; lithium cells up 10% on IRA 45X uncertainty.

Outages up to 4.2% from GE 7FA rotor, $22 million replacement at PJM $250/MWh.

These affirm our Reliable Renewables strategy—25% renewables by year-end balancing nuclear/gas. Challenges stress grid reforms, which we're pushing via EEI. Tailwinds: AI electrification 5-7% load growth to 2027. Raised FY EBITDA to $1.725-1.775 billion, 9-12% growth, Q4 EPS $0.68-0.72.

Building on that operational strength, let's discuss regulatory lag and our mitigation strategies—a key issue amid clean transition, inflation, and grid needs. Regulatory lag is the delay between prudent capex/O&M—like post-Ida/Ian hardening or $1.2 billion BESS—and PUC/FERC recovery via rates/riders. In 2023, it cut authorized ROE 120 bps, $175 million hit across five states.

Regionally: Northeast (2.5 million customers, Eversource-like) sees 18-24 month dockets under CLCPA, lag to 200 bps on offshore wind CWIP. Southeast (Georgia/Florida PSC) faster at 12 months, 85% AFUDC, but $450 million Ian costs mismatched despite riders. EEI: industry lag up 30% since 2021 on 7% CPI, HVDC bottlenecks like NextEra/Dominion.

Lag at quarter-end: $3.8 billion undepreciated net plant, 15% rate base; 65% of $2.7 billion 2023 capex timely vs. 75% five-year average.

Mitigation clawing 40% headwind in 2024: Accelerated filings—Georgia Q3, New York Q4 for $450 million revenue, 100% CWIP on $800 million grid mod with 50,000 AMI, GE Vernova DERMS; biennial reviews cut lag 25%.

Alternative mechanisms: Connecticut MYRP annual adjusts 70% capex like Avangrid/Eversource; Florida PBR pilots add 50 bps ROE on SAIDI/SAIFI via $300 million automation. Southeast solar tracker recovered 92% of $150 million interconnects.

Technical: FERC 2020 queue compliance, $100 million deposits for 1.2 GW renewables; Siemens transformer offtakes hedge 60% 2024-2026 at 15% below spot. Zero-Based O&M saved $120 million via drones/Oracle analytics, offsetting lag.

Hedging: 80% $1.5 billion variable debt swapped at SOFR +150 bps, 5.2% costs. FFO/debt 18-20% aids ATHE/ADIT, 50 bps ROE.

We're trending to 90 bps lag by 2025 vs. S&P median 180 bps, fueling 6-8% EPS growth. Catalysts: PJM BESS awards, New York ZECs add $200 million recoverable. We're turning lag into moat via innovation, EEI advocacy for siting.

Next, our grid modernization and smart grid initiatives, a high-ROI pillar. In FY2023, $650 million capex—up 22% YoY, 18% of T&D—for resilient bidirectional grid across 12 states, PJM to ERCOT/CAISO, handling electrification.

Results: 2.8 million AMI endpoints, 92% penetration vs. EEI 78%; SAIDI down 15% to 85 min/customer, SAIFI 12% to 0.92, saving $42 million O&M via DMS fault isolation. Revenue up 8% or $115 million from TOU/dynamic pricing.

Roadmap: Sensing—1,200 PMUs on 345/138 kV with GE WAMS; caught Polar Vortex deviation in 300 ms, averting 500 MW issue.

Automation: IEEE 1547 at 450 feeders with S&C reclosers/capacitors, 40% faster restoration; Schneider EcoStruxure ADMS for microgrids avoided PSPS in CA heatwaves, islanding 15 MW solar-storage.

Orchestration: AutoGrid DERMS manages 1.2 GW DERs, 250,000 VPP customers; dispatched 180 GWh in Q4 ERCOT post-Elliott, $28 million ancillaries at $155/MWh.

Regional: PJM data centers (20% CAGR) unlocked 300 MW queue via optimization for AWS/Google. ERCOT post-Uri: 500 miles 3M ACCC reconductoring, 25% thermal lift, 150 MW wind. WECC wildfires: Siemens Spectrum Power cut veg mgmt false positives 35%, eyeing $5.5 billion IRA grants.

Returns: 9.5% ROE lift, $0.47/MWh savings. FY2024 $750 million, including $200 million EV: 50,000 ChargePoint Level 2, 200 MW peak shave. BNEF: $105 billion smart grid by 2030, 14% CAGR. Our net-zero grid: IEC 61850 digitalization, NIST cybersecurity vs. threats.

This is our moat for renewables volatility, IRA tailwinds.

Continuing with retirement of fossil fuel plants and replacement strategies, a transformative value play positioning us as top IPP in decarbonizing grids.

Context: Renewables LCOE $25-35/MWh ERCOT solar, EPA MATS/CAA, RPS 50-100% by 2045 CA/NY, gas volatility. EIA: 100 GW coal retired since 2010, 40 GW more to 2030; peakers negative spreads.

Ahead: Announced 1,200 MW coal retirement (Big River, Mill Creek PJM) by 2025 end, six years early—15% thermal, 8% EBITDA. Q2 shut 400 MW Big River, saving $45 million O&M, $120 million fuel. Emissions down 25% to <300 lbs/MWh, net-zero Scope 1&2 by 2040 ahead of Duke/Southern.

Replacements: $4.2 billion capex to 2028, 60% FCF ($650 million Q2 levered, +18% YoY), 40% debt <4%. Renewables anchor: 5 GW hybrids. ERCOT: 1.2 GW solar-storage replaces 800 MW peakers; Rattlesnake 600 MWdc First Solar + 300 MW/1.2 GWh TC Energy LFP, Q4 2025 ops, $32/MWh PPA, 14.5% IRR, 28-30% solar CF to 45%+ stored. 85% queue via deposits.

PJM: 1.8 GW advanced incl. 900 MW Ohio onshore GE 6.0 MW wind, $38/MWh LCOE vs. $55-65 gas. Offshore via 20% Orsted stake, 500 MW NY-like, IRA PTC $0-10/MWh.

Storage: 2.5 GW standalone/hybrid long-duration displaces gas. 200 MW/800 MWh Form Energy iron-air at Mill Creek, 100-hr at 90% eff, $85/kWh 2027, ARPA-E backed, 18% IRR pilot $150 million.

Storage margins: Q2 150 MW/600 MWh CAISO $250/kW-year ancillaries +40% arbitrage, 20%+ unlevered ROE vs. gas 8-10%.

Gas bridge/nuclear: 600 MW H-class GE 7HA.03 Texas, 65% eff CCS-ready, $45/MWh. SMR: 300 MW NuScale VOYGR MISO 2030, DOE guarantees; uprates 1,200 MW nuclear at 93% CF, 70% carbon-free baseload.

Metrics: 8.2 GW queue, 4 GW by 2027; CF 55% to 62%, EBITDA margins +300 bps to 45%, FCF yield 10% on $25 billion EV. Hedged coal divest $200/ton premium; 80% renewables PPAs 2-3% escalators.

Risks hedged: IRA 45X domestic content; 100% contracted polysilicon to 2026. IRA tax 15%. Data center LOIs 1 GW hybrid solar-nuclear $50/MWh.

Regional upsides: ERCOT 50% renewables 2026; PJM RTEP storage blackstart; MISO RA $30/kW-year.

This unlocks $1.2 billion avoided fossil capex, $6 billion EV to 2030. Executing as peers like Vistra/Talen adjust.

Wrapping financial highlights, our capital expenditure for the quarter was $420 million, primarily focused on nuclear uprates and renewable integrations. Balance sheet strong, committed to shareholders. Anticipate EPS growth of 9-11% FY2024, raised guidance.

Finally, on authorized vs. earned ROE analysis, core to our regulatory compact and execution at NovaGen Power Corp. Authorized ROE is PUC/FERC-approved return on rate base; earned is actual NI/equity, weather-normalized per FERC Form 1.

Relevant amid rates, inflation, transition. Our 15 GW regulated fleet—40% gas CC, 30% nuclear, 20% renewables, 10% coal retiring—50,000 miles T&D in PJM/MISO/NYISO funds $4.2 billion five-year capex, A-/A3 ratings, IRA goals.

Trailing 12 months to Sept 30, 2024: authorized 10.25% (Ohio 10.50%, PA 10.00%, FERC trans 10.75%); earned 9.75%—50 bps gap, $45 million on $12.5 billion equity. Better than EEI median 85 bps, our five-year 65 bps.

Trend narrowing: 9.40% earned vs. 10.40% 2020 to now; 2022 Ohio case +75 bps formula; 2023 MISO rider AFUDC $800 million line. Mild winters -10-15 bps offset by PA decoupling.

Regional:
PJM NE (45% rate base): 10.00% auth, 9.90% earned; BRA $270/MW-day gas fleet +20%; EAM O&M -8%.
MISO MW (35%): 10.50% auth, 9.40% earned; lag $1.2 billion renewables (Wind Ridge 400 MW, coal-site batteries); hydro/wind curtail -$20 million offset TRR; Clinton nuclear +15 bps.
FERC trans (15%): 10.75% auth, 11.20% earned; 95% reconductoring ACCC +20% capacity.
Other (5% Ohio dist): parity, EV rebates.

Drivers: Gas hedge $2.75 vs. $3.20 spot +25 bps; digital twins -1.5% heat rates. Neg: depn outpace rate base 200 bps, 18-month lags; pensions -15 bps offset coal sale $150 million.

Allocation: PA default 70% load; Ohio ESP to 2027 PBR SAIDI. 2025 earned 10.05%, 20 bps gap as $900 million new rates, 11.00% MISO request 50th percentile DCF/CAPM at 4.2% Treasuries.

AMI $300 million +30 bps by 2027 DER/pricing; hydrogen gas Siemens, Orsted 1 GW offshore IIJA. ROE-accretive >12% IRR.

50 bps under-earn disciplined amid pressures, improving as regulators see $7 billion clean spend (40% trans, 35% ren/stor, 25% resilience). 6-8% EPS CAGR, dividends, buybacks 60-65% payout. Delivering utility bargain powering transition.

Tom Bradley: Thank you, Maria. On operations, we're seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbine power plants due to AI-driven predictive maintenance. This has resulted in a 5% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 12%, aligning with our Zero-Based Reliability efforts and reduced forced outages from 4.2% through better rotor management and maintenance.

Karen Lee: Thank you, Tom. For long-term strategy, we're exploring opportunities in long-duration battery storage space. This will drive future growth. We're evaluating acquisitions in ERCOT and MISO markets, building on recent Horizon closes and renewables queue advancements.

Raj Singh: Thank you, Karen. Technologically, investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity continue. Recently deployed an AI-powered intrusion detection system to bolster defenses against cyber threats, complementing our PMU/WAMS and NIST hardening.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Maria, Tom, Karen, and Raj. In summary, strong execution across operations, financials, and strategy. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Julien Dumoulin-Smith with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Julien Dumoulin-Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for managing regulatory lag going forward?

Alex Rivera: Certainly, Julien. As Maria detailed, we're tackling lag through accelerated rate filings in Georgia and New York targeting $450 million, full CWIP on grid projects, biennial reviews cutting lag 25%, and mechanisms like MYRP and PBR pilots adding ROE upside. Trackers for renewables and fuel recover costs directly, while operational savings from Zero-Based O&M offset pressures. We've hedged debt and supply chains, trending our lag to 90 bps by 2025, ahead of peers.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Arcaro with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Arcaro: Thanks. What is your outlook for the authorized vs. earned ROE gap?

Maria Gonzalez: Good question, David. We're at 50 bps under-earn now, better than industry 85 bps, and expect to close to 20 bps in 2025 with $900 million new rates flowing, including higher ROE requests justified by DCF/CAPM. Regional over-earns in transmission and efficiencies like hedging and digital twins are helping, alongside formula rates and performance incentives. This supports our 6-8% EPS growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Praful Prasad with Citi. Please go ahead.

Praful Prasad: How are you approaching fossil fuel retirements and replacements amid supply chain issues?

Tom Bradley: Great point, Praful. We've retired 400 MW coal this year, saving significant O&M and fuel, replacing with high-IRR solar-storage hybrids like Rattlesnake at 14.5%, wind, long-duration iron-air batteries, efficient gas, and nuclear/SMRs. Hedged supplies 100% to 2026, IRA credits easing polysilicon/tariffs. Queue at 8.2 GW ensures capacity factors rise to 62%, margins expand, fully funded from FCF and cheap debt.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and commitment to long-term shareholder value. Focused on strategic priorities, positioning NovaGen Power Corp. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
